themes_detail.label: Storm Damage Infrastructure Cascade
themes_detail.summary: Park Slope is experiencing a coordinated surge in infrastructure damage THIS WEEK, with damaged trees up 460% (14 complaints this week vs. 2.5 weekly average), street conditions up 550% (121 complaints last week vs. 18.6 average), and street signs damaged up 567% (5 complaints this week vs. 0.8 average)—suggesting a recent weather event or systematic maintenance failure affecting the neighborhood's public realm.
evidence: Damaged Tree complaints: 14 THIS WEEK vs. 2.5 weekly average (z-score: 9.39)
Street Condition complaints: 121 last week vs. 18.6 weekly average, up 550% (z-score: 12.75)
Street Sign - Damaged complaints: 5 THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average, up 567% (z-score: 6.43)
reporting_angles: Was there a recent storm or high-wind event that triggered these simultaneous complaints?
Interview Parks Department about street tree maintenance protocols and response timeline

themes_detail.label: Explosive Bike Rack/Bike Infrastructure Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Bike Rack complaints skyrocketed 1767% THIS WEEK (7 complaints vs. 0.4 weekly average, z-score: 13.68)—the single largest statistical anomaly in the dataset—alongside a 540% spike in Abandoned Bike complaints (4 this week vs. 0.6 average), suggesting either a new bike-share station deployment, enforcement crackdown, or emerging frustration with cycling infrastructure placement.
evidence: Bike Rack complaints: 7 THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average, up 1767% (z-score: 13.68, highest severity)
Abandoned Bike complaints: 4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average, up 540% (z-score: 6.97)
Both spikes occurred simultaneously in the same week, suggesting a single upstream trigger
reporting_angles: Did Citi Bike or another bike-share operator install new stations or rebalance bikes in Park Slope this week?
Are residents complaining about placement, overcrowding, or lack of racks in specific locations? Map the complaints.

themes_detail.label: Underground Infrastructure Failure Pattern
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints spiked 300% THIS WEEK (20 complaints vs. 5 weekly average, z-score: 6.55) and Water System complaints remain elevated—occurring in parallel with the community board's long-standing request to 'Inspect water main on specific street segment and repair or replace as needed'—suggesting underground infrastructure stress that may require urgent DEP inspection.
evidence: Sewer complaints: 20 THIS WEEK vs. 5 weekly average, up 300% (z-score: 6.55)
Water System complaints remain elevated in top-10 overall (447 complaints over 90 days)
Community Board has repeatedly requested water main inspection and repair on specific street segments—repeating request suggests unresolved baseline problem now accelerating
reporting_angles: Which specific streets are seeing the sewer spikes? Request geo-tagged 311 complaint data to identify clusters.
Contact DEP to determine if water main breaks or combined sewer overflows are occurring; cross-reference with Gowanus Canal CSO Facility completion status

themes_detail.label: Street-Level Noise and Disruption Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street/Sidewalk noise complaints surged 196% last week (34 complaints vs. 11.5 weekly average, z-score: 12.03), suggesting a spike in construction, outdoor events, or vendor activity in Park Slope's pedestrian zones that coincides with the spike in infrastructure complaints—indicating possible large-scale project activity.
evidence: Noise - Street/Sidewalk complaints: 34 last week vs. 11.5 weekly average, up 196% (z-score: 12.03)
Spike coincides with Street Condition and Damaged Tree spikes, suggesting infrastructure work or weather event
Noise complaints overall remain elevated (927 complaints over 90 days across all noise categories)
reporting_angles: Is there an active DOB construction or infrastructure project underway? Cross-reference with 1022 recent permit filings.
Interview residents in blocks with clustered complaints about what they're hearing and when

themes_detail.label: Rodent Complaint Acceleration
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped 182% last week (12 complaints vs. 4.2 weekly average, z-score: 7.11), marking a sharp uptick in pest complaints that may signal either winter migration, sanitation lapses, or new construction activity disrupting populations—worth monitoring for broader infestation trends.
evidence: Rodent complaints: 12 last week vs. 4.2 weekly average, up 182% (z-score: 7.11)
Spike is seasonal but elevated; worth tracking whether it sustains into next weeks
No prior community board budget requests for pest control explicitly listed, but common complaint category
reporting_angles: Interview DOHMH or local pest control about seasonal patterns vs. this week's spike
Map rodent complaints against street condition and sewer spikes—are infrastructure issues creating entry points?
